T.title: Spread the Word Right - Community Builders of Pecan Grove
T.intro: The town hasn't decided yet. The library asked kids to make a 'What we know so far' poster for its board at school. Pick 3 fact cards. Give each one its source and check its date. Then pick a headline. Use one hope and one worry. Add a source and check the date on every card. Your first headline is the one that counts.
T.pickHead: Then pick a headline that tells what is on the poster. Your first pick is the one that counts.
T.tap: Tap a card to put it on the poster.
T.oldLine: Old news from June 2. There is newer news.
T.noSrc: No source. Nobody can show how they know.
T.rumor: This sounds like a rumor. You can take it off.
T.good: Good headline! It tells what's on the poster.
T.sell: This headline tells people what to think. A 'What we know' poster tells what's inside, so everyone can make up their own mind.
T.ask: Ask a grown-up: where can we share it?
T.aha: Sharing a fact without its source or date can spread a mistake.
T.can: I can share facts with their sources and say what we don't know yet.
T.tipRumor: Next time, add a source to every card. If it has no source, it's a rumor. Leave it off.
T.tipSrc: Next time, add the source to every fact before you pin it up.
T.tipDate: Next time, check the date on every card. Old news can sneak in.
T.tipMix: Next time, show a hope and a worry, so every neighbor feels heard.
T.tipHead: Next time, pick a headline that tells what's inside, not what to think.
T.tip100: Great poster! Try a new round with new cards.
T.real: Make a poster for your class or library, with permission. Every fact gets its source and date. No posting online.
T.guText: Kids make a poster with sources and dates, show a hope and a worry, and choose a safe place to share it: family, class, or a library board with permission. No social media, petitions or campaign materials.
T.checkEach: Add a source and check the date on every card.
T.readyPin: You can pin it up now.
